title: Encryption: who can decrypt your data, and what must you start for post-quantum?
short: Automate certificate renewal before the 100-day limit on 15 March 2027, and inventory your cryptography for the post-quantum move.
answer: Automate renewal of every public TLS certificate before the maximum lifetime drops to 100 days on 15 March 2027[^br], and inventory your cryptography this quarter so data that must stay secret for ten years or more gets hybrid post-quantum key exchange first. Then judge each measure by who can use the key, and whether you could still decrypt if it were deleted.
audience: IT, security and platform teams in EU organizations that run TLS, certificates, disk and database encryption, cloud key management and secrets

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Automate certificate renewal by March 2027.
items.text: Public TLS certificates issued from 15 March 2027 may last at most 100 days[^br]. Renew with ACME and let ACME Renewal Information (ARI) set the timing, not a fixed interval[^le45]. Alert a week before any expiry.

items.title: Inventory your cryptography.
items.text: List TLS endpoints, certificates, keys and who holds them, algorithms and trust stores. The EU roadmap calls this a no-regret first step that needn't be complete before you set priorities[^eufaq].

items.title: Turn on hybrid post-quantum key exchange.
items.text: Recorded traffic can be decrypted once a large quantum computer exists, so BSI recommends hybrid key agreement for long-term secrets[^tr1] and accepts `X25519MLKEM768` in TLS 1.3[^bsitr]. Chrome, Firefox and Apple's version 26 systems offer it[^chrome][^ffpq][^apple].

items.title: Separate who manages keys from who uses them.
items.text: AWS KMS key administrators can't use a key but can rewrite its policy to grant themselves access[^kmspol]. Activate key admin roles just in time, with approval[^akvsec].

items.title: Get secrets out of code and into a vault.
items.text: Give apps managed identities, not stored credentials, and one vault per app and environment[^akvsec]. Rotate any exposed secret at once. For CI tokens, see the supply-chain sheet.

items.title: Which data must stay secret for ten years or more?
items.text: The EU roadmap counts it as high-risk and wants it protected from quantum attacks by the end of 2030[^euroadmap]. Think of health and HR records, contracts, designs and their backups.

items.title: Where does it travel and where is it stored?
items.text: Follow it through load balancers, VPNs, SSH, APIs, databases and backups, including systems your managed service providers run.

items.title: What protects it, and who holds the key?
items.text: Record the protocol and key exchange, the certificate and issuer, where the key lives (HSM, cloud KMS or a file) and who can use it. AWS load balancer connection logs record the negotiated key exchange[^albpol].

items.title: Which trust stores do your systems rely on?
items.text: List the CA bundle in each runtime, container image and appliance, and how each one gets updated. For Python, see the secure-python sheet.

items.title: What can't be upgraded?
items.text: Ask suppliers when they will support ML-KEM. BSI strongly recommends that products expected to run beyond 2030 can be upgraded to quantum-safe methods[^tr1].

blocks.title: TLS baseline
items: **Offer TLS 1.3 and 1.2 only.** BSI prefers TLS 1.3, recommends TLS 1.2 only until the end of 2031 and doesn't recommend TLS 1.0 or 1.1[^tr2].

**Put hybrid groups first.** List `X25519MLKEM768` ahead of `X25519`, as OpenSSL 3.5 does by default[^ossl35]. Recent Windows 11 and Server 2025 builds support it in Schannel but leave it off; enable it with the ECC Curve Order group policy[^schannel]. On AWS load balancers, pick `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-Res-PQ-2025-09`[^albpol].
**Meet BSI key lengths.** Prefer ECDSA P-256 keys. BSI wants RSA keys of at least 3000 bits, so the usual RSA 2048 falls short[^tr2].

blocks.title: Who holds the keys
items: **Encryption at rest stops disk thieves, not logins.** It protects against someone with the hardware but not the key[^azrest]. S3 decrypts for any authenticated request with permission[^s3sse].
**Platform-managed keys suit most data,** Microsoft says[^azrest]. Choose customer-managed keys for specific regulatory or security needs; their availability becomes your job.
**Make deletion slow and keep backups.** Turn on Key Vault soft delete and purge protection, back up keys that can't be recreated and test the restore[^akvsec].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **A certificate authority lost its keys.** In October 2026 eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys proved recoverable. Mozilla dropped trust in eMudhra's emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and Chrome committed to do the same[^emudhra]. Update the trust store in every runtime and image, and keep a second ACME CA ready.
**Public certificates are becoming server-only.** Chrome requires public certificates issued from 15 March 2027 to be for server authentication only[^crp]. Move mutual TLS to a private CA.
**BSI and NIST set end dates for classical cryptography** in TR-02102 2026-01 and the final IR 8547 (dates below)[^tr1][^ir8547].

items.name: Public TLS certificates
items.scope: Maximum lifetime and domain validation reuse, binding on every public CA[^br].

items.name: Post-quantum migration
items.scope: EU roadmap milestones[^euroadmap], with BSI and NIST dates.

steps.what: BSI: TLS 1.2 and classical-only key exchange end[^tr1][^tr2]
Medium-risk migrated[^euroadmap]; NIST bars RSA and ECC[^ir8547]

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Bigger symmetric keys for quantum.** NIST believes approved symmetric algorithms with at least 128-bit security meet its lowest post-quantum security category[^ir8547].

**Post-quantum TLS certificates now.** Classical signatures stay trustworthy until a quantum computer exists, and BSI recommends them until the end of 2035[^tr1]. Firmware signing can't wait that long[^euroadmap].
**Cloud keys in an external key store.** AWS says their availability and latency risks exceed the perceived benefit for most customers[^xks].
**Rotating KMS keys more than yearly.** Wrapping keys are almost never used enough to wear out[^kmsrot].

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Deleting a key something still uses.** A deleted AWS KMS key leaves its data unrecoverable. Disable it first and alarm on use during the 7 to 30 day waiting period[^kmsdel].

**Trusting infrastructure-as-code defaults.** AWS load balancer listeners created from the CLI, CloudFormation or CDK without a named policy get `ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08`, which allows TLS 1.0 and 1.1[^albpol].

**Turning off post-quantum key exchange for a middlebox.** Firefox warns this removes protection against later decryption of recorded traffic[^ffpq], and Chrome's switch for it ended after version 146[^chrome]. Fix the middlebox.

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Use your host's or CDN's managed certificates, or an ACME client with ARI, and turn on expiry alerts.
Keep the cloud's default encryption, and keep passwords and API keys in a vault, not in code.
Ask your IT provider and SaaS vendors when they will support hybrid post-quantum TLS.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Build the inventory from load balancer logs, certificate transparency and config scans; give every certificate and key an owner.
Enable hybrid ML-KEM on internet-facing TLS and SSH, and watch logs for clients that fall back.
Run a private CA for client certificates and put key admin roles behind just-in-time access.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Write the cryptography policy NIS2 requires. For cloud and other digital providers, Regulation 2024/2690 sets its content, from algorithms to key destruction[^enisa].
Keep the inventory in a standard format such as CBOM[^euroadmap] and report quantum risk to the board.
Start with the PKI, the slowest to migrate, and put PQC support into supplier contracts.
